header: First line of every Agent prompt: AGENT: type=<type> model=<model> why=<one-line justification>. The Agent tool's `model` parameter must be set to the same model (agents inherit the parent's Opus otherwise).
override: A model outside `allowed` for the type is an override: the hook asks the user (permission prompt). Forks always ask.

search.use_for: find files / symbols / usages, read-only sweeps (single lookups: Grep/Read directly, no agent)

run.use_for: launch or queue jobs from a written recipe, regenerate reports from data, collect results

report.use_for: summarise finished results into tables / notes (Codex luna via cdx-agent --offload is cheaper)

code-fix.use_for: well-specified change, files and tests known (Codex luna via cdx-agent is the cheaper first choice)

implement.use_for: new flag / feature / script over a few files, with tests

debug.use_for: find the cause of a failure from logs / data / code

design.use_for: architecture, experiment design, plans with trade-offs

wait.use_for: never an agent: run_in_background shell loop, then cdx-agent --offload for the summary

safety-review.use_for: independent re-derivation of safety/dynamics math (constraints, bounds, certificates); seed with `cdx-agent --brief TARGET --focus safety-math`, never with the author's conclusions; no forks

effort_note: The Agent tool's `effort` parameter: when omitted the gate sets the type default (updatedInput); above the type max it asks the user (override), like models.
